Appreciate the clear ask. I’m putting together a concise evidence pack and the team’s recommendations. Short answers up front:

- For Redwood Private deployed inside a customer VPC (customer-managed runtime), outbound egress is typically under customer control (NAT or egress gateway). Redwood does not implicitly publish a fixed set of public egress IPs for customers' private runtimes by default.

Quick technical notes (will drop into the spreadsheet):

- Deployment model distinction:
  * Customer-managed runtime (typical VPC/on-prem install): all outbound egress exits your NAT or egress gateway. Customer is owner of the public IPs.
  * Redwood-managed egress (opt-in): Redwood operates an outbound proxy/NAT for control-plane callbacks and telemetry; we can assign static IPs but this requires a commercial add-on and cross-account peering for log ingestion (see Marissa).

- Minimum firewall rules (customer-managed egress):
  * Destination: api-control.redwood.ai (TLS 443) — purpose: control-plane callbacks and rollout checks — Owner: Redwood (if you allow outbound to our control plane) — TLS: required; SNI: api-control.redwood.ai
  * Destination: telemetry.ingest.redwood.ai (TLS 443) — purpose: metrics/log uploads — Owner: optional (Redwood if you allow telemetry) — TLS: required; ALPN: h2 preferred
  * Destination: model-catalog.redwood.ai (443) and S3-backed URIs for weights/plugins — purpose: model version downloads — Owner: Redwood/Customer (depends on private blob storage) — TLS required; use FQDN rather than fixed IPs where possible
  * DNS: outbound to customer DNS resolvers as configured; if you use split-horizon, ensure model-catalog redirections resolve correctly

- IP guidance: we prefer FQDN+TLS (SNI) allowlists. If Acme requires IP-level allowlisting, we can produce a short-term export of egress IPs for Redwood-managed egress; for customer-managed egress the public IPs will be whatever your NAT reports (we can provide diagnostic traffic patterns to validate).

- Ports: 443 outbound for control/telemetry/model fetch; ephemeral ports for callbacks are initiated from customer side in most installs (so firewall does not need inbound allowances).

I’ll prepare the technical tab of the spreadsheet and send back by EOD.

—Ben

Hi Jennifer —

Thanks for the request and patience. Attached is a filled evidence sheet tailored for Acme (egress-evidence-acme-v1.xlsx) and a short summary of ownership and recommended firewall rules. Highlights:

- Ownership model: customer-managed egress is our default and recommended for full network control. If you prefer Redwood to own outbound IPs we offer a Redwood-managed egress add-on (requires a brief contract amendment).

- Recommended allowlist (customer-managed):
  * FQDN: api-control.redwood.ai — Purpose: control-plane callbacks/health checks — TLS 1.2+ required; SNI matching api-control.redwood.ai
  * FQDN: telemetry.ingest.redwood.ai — Purpose: metrics/log upload — TLS with ALPN h2 preferred
  * FQDN: model-catalog.redwood.ai and S3 endpoints — Purpose: model artifact download — TLS required; where possible allow by FQDN wildcard for the storage provider used
  * Ports: 443 outbound. No inbound firewall openings are required for normal operation.

- IP-level option: if your compliance team insists on static IPs, we can provide a signed export of outbound IPs only if you consume Redwood-managed egress. For customer-managed NATs, the public IPs are controlled by your NAT; we can provide sample curl traces and a short validation playbook to help your auditors.

- TLS/mTLS: standard TLS is used for control and telemetry. We support mutual TLS for high-security customers on request (requires certificate exchange and short config window).

Next steps: I uploaded the spreadsheet and supporting notes to a shared Drive (link below). If you confirm whether you want Redwood-managed egress, I’ll include a concrete list of IPs and an SLA note. Otherwise, the attached spreadsheet should be sufficient for your audit to document owner = Acme, egress = customer NAT.

Shared evidence link: https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/AcmeHealth/egress-evidence

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the sheet with your NetOps team.

Best,
David Kim
Senior Solutions Architect, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachment: egress-evidence-acme-v1.xlsx
